study.title: The Role of Medial Prefrontal Cortex in Acupuncture Treatment for Functional Dyspepsia
study.study_design: secondary data analysis of two randomized controlled neuroimaging trials
study.randomization: randomization performed in the original trials (ChiCTR-IOR-15006402 and ChiCTR-IOR-15006523); this study is a secondary analysis
study.blinding: not_reported for this secondary analysis; original trials had controlled designs
study.population: FD patients from the outpatient department of the Affiliated Hospital of Chengdu University of Traditional Chinese Medicine and the campus of Chengdu University of Traditional Chinese Medicine
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) they match the Rome III criteria for functional dyspepsia and postprandial distress syndrome, (2) they are right-handed and aged 18 to 45 years old, (3) they are not attending any other clinical trials in last 3 months, and (4) they provide written informed consent
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) had esophagitis, gastric atrophy, or erosive gastroduodenal lesions on endoscopy; cholecystitis; and gallstones; (2) were pregnant or lactating; (3) were suffering from cardiovascular, renal, or respiratory illnesses or other organic diseases; (4) had a history of psychiatric and neurological disorders or head trauma with loss of consciousness; or (5) were using dynamic gastrointestinal medicine or received acupuncture treatment during the last 15 metal stents or electronic implant, intraocular metal foreign body, claustrophobia, hyperpyrexia, etc.

extraction_notes.note: This is a secondary analysis of two original RCTs. The arms described here (all FD, higher response, lower response) are derived from pooling and post-hoc subgrouping of data from the two original trials (ChiCTR-IOR-15006402 and ChiCTR-IOR-15006523). Each original trial had multiple arms (e.g., ST36+CV12 vs ST36 alone vs CV12 alone; ST36 with Deqi vs ST36 without Deqi). This secondary analysis does not separately report these original arm-level comparisons but pools all 115 FD patients receiving acupuncture.

Scanner manufacturer, model, field strength, TR, TE, and scan duration are not reported in this secondary analysis paper. These parameters are stated to be the same across all subjects and reference the original trial protocols (Yin et al., 2017; Sun et al., 2018).

No sham acupuncture arm is analyzed in this secondary study. The original trials included control conditions (ST36 alone, CV12 alone, no-Deqi), but these are not analyzed in the neuroimaging comparisons presented here.
Expectancy, blinding success, and credibility were not assessed or reported in this paper.
Adverse events are not reported in this paper.

Table 1 labels 'Frontal_Mid' as 'middle temporal gyrus' in the table footnote, which may be an inconsistency or labeling convention in the original paper. The region labeled Frontal_Mid R at MNI 39, 21, 51 is more anatomically consistent with middle frontal gyrus; however, the table footnote explicitly states 'Frontal_Mid, middle temporal gyrus'. This apparent inconsistency is preserved as reported.

The paper describes the correlation between mPFC change and NDSI improvement as 'the more significant the decrease in mPFC activity, the more influential the dyspepsia symptoms' in the discussion, while the results describe an increase in mPFC and r=0.20, p=0.03 as a positive correlation. The exact directionality of the correlation as written in the results (increase correlated with improvement) is preserved.

Cluster size units (voxels vs. mm^3) are not explicitly stated in the tables. 'Cluster size' column values are extracted as reported; unit labeled as 'voxels (inferred)' based on typical DPARSF/SPM reporting conventions.

The between-group comparison method for mPFC rsFC changes (Table 6, Figure 5) is not fully specified (e.g., independent samples t-test vs. ANCOVA). The paper describes it as 'a comparison of the mPFC rsFC in the higher response and lower response groups'.

The exclusion criteria text appears partially corrupted in the PDF ('during the last 15 metal stents or electronic implant') — likely a missing phrase referencing a duration period and then MRI contraindications. Copied as reported from the PDF.

The paper reports the correlation p-value for Frontal_Sup_Medial R (MNI 9, 48, 48) as 0.03* and for Frontal_Sup_Medial R (MNI 12, 63, 12) as 0.11 in Table 1. These appear to be two separate peak coordinates for the same atlas label but different cluster locations. Both are extracted as separate rows.

The paper does not explicitly state that the coordinate space is MNI for all tables, but the header of Table 1 explicitly states 'MNI' and 'Montreal Neurological Institute' in the footnote, so MNI is applied to all coordinate rows.
Deqi sensation ratings during treatment are not quantitatively reported in this secondary analysis paper, though one of the original trials (Sun et al., 2018) compared Deqi vs no-Deqi conditions.
